path_used: MCP path: @next-ai-drawio/mcp-server@0.4.6 (bundled offline draw.io) driven over stdio by a small node client (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk Client + StdioClientTransport), env PORT=4314 BROWSER=none DRAWIO_DATA_DIR=off. Tools called: start_session -> create_new_diagram(xml) -> export_diagram(.drawio) -> export_diagram(.png). The preview page (required for PNG export) was opened in headless Chromium from /opt/pw-browsers via playwright-core. Claude wrote the mxCell XML (generated by small Python layout scripts). Export is 2x scale + 20px margin; PNG then downscaled with PIL (LANCZOS) to 1080x1350 / 1080x1080 / 1600x900. Fallback (jgraph/drawio webapp on 4314) was NOT needed.

setup.disk: 100M (node_modules: mcp-server incl. bundled draw.io, MCP SDK, playwright-core)
steps: read README + dist/index.js to learn tool schemas (export needs a connected preview tab)
write client.mjs (stdio MCP client + headless Chromium opening the preview URL)
call start_session to fetch the drawing guide
smoke test render with Vietnamese text (OK, diacritics render)
problems: PNG/SVG export is rendered by the browser preview tab, so a headless browser has to be kept open on the session URL; with BROWSER=none the server does not open one itself
export has no scale/size option: always 2x + fixed 20px margin, so exact canvas size was obtained by drawing a full-size white background rectangle (target minus 40px) and downscaling
drawing guide suggests keeping diagrams within 800x600, ignored to hit the required canvas sizes

fixes: attempt1: layout OK (vertical axis, alternating cards, 3 phase pills on axis, 9->6 dashed loop via right margin, 12->start loop via bottom+left margin); text looked small
attempt2: larger title/desc font (20/15), wider cards (350), margins narrowed -> left loop label wrapped badly
attempt3: manual line breaks in descriptions 2,3,8 to avoid orphan words; shortened loop label text
limits: 12->start loop arrow ends at the 'Giai doan 1' pill rather than directly on step 1
9->6 arrow has to cross the central axis (6 and 9 are on opposite sides by the alternating rule)
step 4 has no description in the data; a short one was added ('người thật xem và chốt chiến lược')

fixes: attempt1 (after a pre-render fix of an angle bug in my generator): circle with 12 numbered dots clockwise, 3 phase arcs (mxgraph.basic.partConcEllipse) separated by gaps with phase pills, curved sequential arrows, inner loop arrows; human label boxes overflowed and text wraps had orphan words
attempt2: human titles split on 2 lines, taller human boxes, wider labels, moved loop label closer to its arrow -> step 4 box went 2px past the canvas
attempt3: manual line breaks in descriptions, step 4/9 boxes realigned inside canvas
limits: labels outside the ring limit the circle size; noticeable empty band at top of the square
phase arcs are a light track partly hidden behind the arrows; curved edges only approximate a circle (quadratic spline through one control point)
12->1 loop drawn inside the ring (replaces the 12->1 ring segment)

fixes: attempt1: 3 background phase columns, 2 lanes (vertical lane labels 'AI làm' / 'Người duyệt'), 10 AI cards in one row, steps 4 and 9 in the bottom lane under 3 and 8, orthogonal arrows, dashed 9->6 back arrow in bottom lane, 12->1 loop over the top; titles wrapped unevenly

attempt3: larger fonts (17/14) and narrower cards for longer inter-card arrows -> regression: human card titles '4. Người duyệt chiến lược' / '9. Người duyệt nội dung' now wrap onto 3 lines and step 4 text nearly fills its box; kept as final because the 3-attempt cap was reached
limits: 10 AI steps in one row at 1600px forces narrow cards (132px) and small text; horizontal arrows between cards are very short
large empty areas in the 'Người duyệt' lane

notes: peak_ram_mb from measure.py is ru_maxrss of the largest single child process (node MCP server/client or Chromium), not the sum of the process tree; each render step = start MCP server + headless Chromium + create + 2 exports (~10 s)
No LLM API used: Claude wrote all XML; outputs not self-scored
